ESTENZO Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson Barangay Guadalupe, Cebu City Dear SK Chairperson Estenzo: This pertains to your earlier letter, addressed to Dr. Nelia N. Aquino, CESO, City Director, DILG Cebu City, forwarded to Central Office, requesting for guidance on the following queries which stemmed from the failure of an elected SK member to timely file his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE): I. Can the said SK member receive his monthly honorarium even if he has not assumed office and was deemed absent during regular sessions? 2. Can he receive financial subsidy coming from the city? 3. Can he sign resolutions and other official documents given he has not received any certificate of compliance from the Commission on Elections? 4. Should they submit the same report to the office of the DILG and SK Federation for their information and reference? We discuss. As to your@_st_queuy, we opine that the office of an elected candidate who failed to file his/her SOCE shall be considered "vacant" until he/she complied with the requirement for assumption into office. Such vacancy is considered a temporary vacancy which shall be filled up in accordance with Section 19(c) of Republic Act No. 10742, otherwise known as the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015, as amended by Republic Act No. 11768. As to the entitlement to the payment of monthly honorarium, the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM), defines honorarium as that "remuneration given to public official for services actually rendered". Hence, the grant of honorarium is based principally on services actually rendered by the claimant thereof. Should the SK official fail to file the required SOCE within 30 days after election, he/she cannot enter upon the duties of his/her office and discharge his/her functions, and is therefore not entitled to the payment of the monthly honorarium in the absence of required actual services rendered. With regard to the secgnd_guety, we advise to direct your concern to the concerned office of the City Government of Cebu as the grant of such allowance would depend on the guidelines of the issuing LGU. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

For the tOir-d-gu-e.!Y, we answer in the negative. As previously stated, no elected official shall enter upon the duties of office until he/she filed his SOCE. Hence, the concerned SK member may not be allowed to sign resolutions and other official documents of the SK. Finally, as to the please be advised that that the Department issued DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2023-1651, dated 27 March 2023 which "revokes the requirement that a newly elected official submits to the DILG, before assuming office, a Certification from COMELEC of SOCE Filing". In view thereof, the submission to SOCE report to the DILG is no longer necessary. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs 1 Revocation of Additional Requirement to Submit to DILG a Certification from COMELEC of Filing of Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE).
